sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Strings are everywhere in programming - from user input to file handling. Today, you'll master the essential String class methods that make text manipulation a breeze!

• How to use common String methods like `length()`, `charAt()`, and `substring()`
• The magic of string concatenation and comparison
• Practical ways to transform and search strings

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine strings as a row of connected train cars. Each car holds one character, and you can:
- Count how many cars there are (length)
- Peek inside any car (charAt)
- Take a segment of cars (substring)

Strings in Java are objects with powerful built-in tools (methods) to work with text. Unlike primitive types, they come with their own set of superpowers!

• **Immutable**: Once created, strings can't be changed (but you can create new ones)
• **Zero-indexed**: First character is at position 0, not 1
• **Method-rich**: Over 50 useful methods available at your fingertips

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how String methods work:

steps.title: Creating a String
steps.description: When you create a string, Java stores it in memory with each character at a specific index.

steps.title: Accessing Characters
steps.description: Use `charAt()` to peek at any character like opening a specific train car.

steps.title: Extracting Substrings
steps.description: Use `substring()` to take a segment of the string, like cutting a section of train cars.

steps.title: String Length
steps.description: Count all characters with `length()`, like counting all train cars.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Strings are immutable - methods return new strings rather than modifying the original
✓ Indexes start at 0, not 1 (first character is at position 0)
✓ `substring()` is inclusive of start index but exclusive of end index
✓ Always check string length before accessing characters to avoid errors

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `trim()` to remove unwanted whitespace from user input
Combine methods like `toLowerCase().contains()` for case-insensitive searches
donts: Don't use `==` to compare strings (it compares references, not content)
Don't create too many string objects in loops (use StringBuilder instead)
sections.protip: For frequent string modifications, use `StringBuilder` - it's like having a train where you can add/remove cars without building a whole new train!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: String methods are used everywhere in real applications:

examples.how: Using `contains("@")` and `endsWith(".com")` to check email formats
Using `toLowerCase()` and `indexOf()` to find keywords in web pages
Using `length()`, `matches()` with regex to validate password requirements
Using `split()` to break CSV files into individual values

problem.description:
Write a method that takes a full name (e.g., "John Michael Doe") and returns the initials (e.g., "JMD"). The method should:
1. Handle any number of names
2. Work with mixed case input
3. Ignore extra spaces
hints: Use `split()` to break the name into parts
Use `charAt(0)` to get the first character of each part
problem.explanation: We first trim extra spaces and split the name into parts. Then we take the first character of each part, combine them, and convert to uppercase. The `StringBuilder` efficiently builds our result string.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Strings are objects with powerful built-in methods for text manipulation
📌 Practice combining methods for more complex operations
📌 Ready to learn about `StringBuilder` for more efficient string modifications!
